# Orca orchestration: supervise multi-agent workers

Curated by Skill Harbor — @stablyai's orchestration skill for the Orca CLI: a structured way to run supervised multi-agent work — threaded messages between agents, blocking ask/reply flows, task dispatch with worker_done/escalation waits, task DAGs, decision gates, coordinator loops, and decomposing work across agents and worktrees. By design this file is a discovery stub: the full version-matched orchestration reference is served live by the `orca` binary itself (`ORCA skills get orchestration`) so the guide can never drift from the binary that actually runs your commands. Honest caveats: requires a working Orca runtime (the skill helps you resolve the right executable — `orca-dev`, `orca-ide` or `orca` — and warns against Linux's GNOME Orca screen reader of the same name); MIT-licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
